result.rationale: The trajectory shows the rescue team repeatedly failing to reach/act on the two civilians (Kade at life-console, Sato at med-ward) because of spatial and hostile pressure. Engineer Imani is repeatedly damaged by Raider Holt's scatter-blast (100→71→46) and by the reactor environment hazard (46→36→26→16), while reactor-heat climbs 62→70→78→86→94→100. Medic Reyes successfully escorts Sato at turn 3, but then at turn 4 his move to junction-cover is contested (target_zone_capacity_lost), blocking the extraction route. Security Chen is also drained by reactor environment damage (110→100→90→80→55→45). The core bottleneck is that hostile/environmental spatial pressure (Raider Holt's attacks, reactor-instability hazard, zone capacity contestation) prevents the actors from converting the available rescue affordances (both civilians located, Sato escorted) into extraction progress. This is a survival/spatial-pressure bottleneck rather than an information or policy problem: the civilians are known and reachable, but health, position, and capacity pressure block the useful action.
